assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, turned laser-cooled atoms into a frequency standard with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. It is a measurement instrument that opened a new regime for metrology, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. Clear, original and lasting, and the kind of patient calibration-and-systematics work I respect.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the lattice clock with strontium. Ye's group drove it to the accuracy frontier and made the first resolved-sideband and many-body clock advances. The two-person configuration looks fair. Others (for example Lemonde, Hollberg, Hall and Hänsch on the comb) were recognised earlier or sit outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups (JILA, RIKEN, SYRTE, PTB, NIST) have confirmed the technique, and the interpretation is stable. Timely; the redefinition of the SI second is being prepared.
uncertainties: The relative weight of Katori's proposal against Ye's accuracy work is a judgement I cannot verify independently.
Part of the field's recognition already went to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, so the committee may see this as too incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BeppoSAX's arcsecond X-ray localisations led to the first X-ray and optical afterglows and then redshifts, proving gamma-ray bursts are cosmological. This settled a 30-year debate and founded multi-wavelength burst astronomy. It rests on instrument capability (wide-field cameras plus rapid pointing) and is close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228. Kulkarni's team had the decisive optical, redshift and radio follow-up. Van Paradijs (deceased) and others made decisive contributions, so a three-person prize is defensible but leaves real attribution tension. I have not independently verified the exact credit splits.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed many times over by Swift, HETE-2 and ground follow-up, and the interpretation (relativistic fireball, cosmological distances) is stable. Recognition is somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among BeppoSAX, optical and radio teams is contested, and the deceased contributors cannot be honoured.
Prior recognition (Shaw, Gruber and others) may reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene launched moire quantum materials. Importance, originality and breadth of follow-on work are very large. Condensed matter is outside my expertise, so I rely on colleagues for the physics detail.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle in 2011. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiments. Cao, Fatemi and others who did the 2018 measurements are not in the credit, which raises a fair-allocation question. Other twisted-graphene groups (Dean, Young, Yacoby, Ju) matter too.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced by many groups, with many follow-on phases. Still evolving, so a few more years could clarify which discoveries are lasting.
uncertainties: Several moire phenomena remain debated, and the scope of the prize (theory plus experiment) is unsettled.
The credit omits the early-career experimentalists who did the 2018 work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations gave a standard ruler imprinted in galaxy clustering. The SDSS and 2dFGRS detections in 2005 turned this into a precision probe of dark energy and expansion history. A measurement-driven discovery with lasting impact, now central to DESI and Euclid.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein's SDSS luminous-red-galaxy detection and the 2dFGRS analysis by Cole, Percival and colleagues were simultaneous and independent. Credit is shared across large survey collaborations, and the supplied three-person set is reasonable but leaves out other key people (e.g. Peebles-Yu and Sunyaev-Zeldovich theory predate it).
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by SDSS, 2dFGRS, WiggleZ, BOSS, eBOSS and DESI. Interpretation is stable, though recent DESI hints on evolving dark energy are open.
uncertainties: Theory priority from Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich is outside the credited set.
Survey-collaboration size makes individual attribution hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube, plus the 2018 TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane result, opened neutrino astronomy at PeV energies. This is a big-instrument achievement, with a detector built in Antarctic ice. As an astroparticle physicist I regard it as a strong candidate.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, but the supplied credit lists him alone. A fair prize would normally include other IceCube pioneers (e.g. instrument builders and AMANDA leaders), who are not in the supplied credit. I can only propose Halzen from the list, and I flag that as a weakness.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established. Source identification is still limited (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane at a few to 4 sigma-level), so the astrophysical picture is maturing, not settled.
uncertainties: The single-name credit cannot support a fair multi-person allocation by itself.
Source-level evidence is still limited and awaits KM3NeT and IceCube-Gen2 confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean quantum many-body Hamiltonians. The Zoller-Jaksch proposal and the Greiner-Bloch superfluid-to-Mott transition made a programmable quantum simulator. Importance and influence are very high, though AMO and many-body theory are outside my expertise.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided the theory proposal, and Bloch and Greiner the decisive experiments. Cirac and Jaksch are other plausible names, so the three-person limit forces a hard choice. I defer to colleagues on how to weigh theory against experiment.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across many groups, including quantum gas microscopes. The method is mature and its interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: The three-person limit excludes Cirac, who is credited elsewhere on the list, and Jaksch.
I cannot assess the many-body physics at an expert level.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84) provides key exchange with security based on physics, and has led to real satellite and fibre links. Conceptually original and clearly lasting, with concrete applications I find convincing.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84, which is the decisive step. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a separate and influential contribution; a prize could reasonably take two or three names. I have chosen two as the cleanest allocation.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated over fibre and satellite links, and commercial systems exist. Security proofs for practical devices are still being refined, but the idea is well settled.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement could make the committee cautious.
Real-device side-channel vulnerabilities remain a concern about practical impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing arrays gave evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries. A natural fit for my taste: precision timing instruments and patient control of systematics.
assessment.attribution: NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA and InPTA all contribute and the decisive credit is spread across collaborations. McLaughlin, Kramer and Manchester are reasonable leaders of three of them but are not an obvious or complete choice.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is at about 3 to 4 sigma with Hellings-Downs correlation, and the source of the signal is not yet established. It is likely premature until the combined IPTA data reaches a firm detection.
uncertainties: The signal origin (black-hole binaries versus new physics) is unresolved.
Attribution across several collaborations is unstable.
